content: Sodium borate is an over-the-counter (OTC) medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of canker sores (mouth ulcers). Common adverse reactions associated with its use include vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and rash. For adults and children, the recommended dosage is to dissolve 5 pellets under the tongue three times a day until symptoms are relieved or as directed by a physician. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of sodium borate in both adults and pediatric patients, whether guideline-supported or not. Contraindications for sodium borate are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include stopping use and consulting a physician if symptoms persist for more than three days or worsen. The product should be kept out of reach of children and not used if the pellet dispenser seal is broken. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and rash. Postmarketing experience data is limited. Information on drug interactions is also scarce. For specific populations, there is no FDA guidance on the use of sodium borate during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals are advised to consult a healthcare professional before use. Similarly, there is no FDA guidance on its use in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised populations. Sodium borate is administered orally. There is limited information on monitoring, IV compatibility, overdose, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. Clinical studies and details on how the product is supplied are also not well-documented. The product should be stored at room temperature. The active ingredient in sodium borate is not specified, but inactive ingredients include lactose and sucrose. There is no established interaction between alcohol and sodium borate, but patients are advised to discuss alcohol use with their doctor. The brand name for sodium borate is BORAX®, and there is limited information on look-alike drug names.
